faq.title: The questions people ask us before downloading

items.question: How long does a parcel take to arrive?
items.answer: The length of the flight, plus the time it takes to agree a meeting with the recipient. You see the traveller's departure and arrival dates before you book: you are the one choosing the trip that suits you. We do not advertise a standard delivery time, because there is no delivery round behind it: there is a flight, taken by a real person.

items.question: How much does it cost to send something?
items.answer: The traveller sets their price per kilo based on their trip and what they agree to carry. A service fee is added on top, always shown before you pay. For a 5 kg parcel with a traveller at 8 euros per kilo, the traveller receives 40 euros and you pay 40 euros plus the fee.

items.question: What am I not allowed to send?
items.answer: Drugs and narcotics, weapons, explosives and hazardous materials, counterfeits or goods prohibited by customs, live animals, official documents (passports, identity cards, residence permits), and any item prohibited by the law of the departure, destination or transit country. Before confirming a shipment you electronically sign a warning about prohibited goods and your customs liability; the traveller reviews your full declaration and can refuse a non-compliant parcel at handover.

items.question: When am I charged?
items.answer: By card, your payment is authorised when you send your request and charged when the traveller accepts it. The money then stays held on the platform: the traveller only receives it once delivery is confirmed with the 6-digit code, which you pass on to the recipient yourself. If the traveller declines or the shipment is cancelled before handover, you get a full refund, fee included. With cash, you pay the traveller directly.

items.question: What if the parcel never arrives?
items.answer: Report it from the app: a dispute can be opened within 15 days of the planned date. While it is being reviewed, the payout to the traveller stays on hold. The team reviews the scans, photos and in-app messages and rules within 72 business hours. Yadony may refund all or part of the shipment, up to a cap and under the conditions shown in the app.

items.question: How much does a traveller earn?
items.answer: Their full asking price. The service fee is paid by the sender, on top of the traveller's price. Nothing is paid out before delivery is confirmed, and the bank transfer then follows your bank's usual timing.

items.question: What happens if there is a customs check?
items.answer: The traveller declares what they are carrying. In the app, every parcel comes with a description and the photos taken at handover, which they can show. Any duties and taxes remain payable by the sender. That is also the reason for the list of prohibited items: a parcel held up at customs holds up the person carrying it.

items.question: Which cities are covered?
items.answer: You freely pick the departure and arrival cities, in France, Europe, Africa or elsewhere. The most frequent trips link Paris, Lyon and Marseille with Abidjan, Dakar, Bamako and Douala, in both directions.

seo.title: Trust and safety: verified identity, escrow payment, disputes
seo.description: How yadony secures a parcel between individuals: identity checks with Didit, payment held until delivery, a 6-digit handover code, a dispute process and data handling.

trust.title: What the platform guarantees, and what it does not
trust.lead: This page describes the mechanisms in place, without dressing them up. If something here looks insufficient to you, write to us: it is more useful to say so now than to find out when something goes wrong.

identity.title: Identity verification
identity.text: No unverified account can post a trip or a parcel request. Each user sends an ID document and a selfie to Didit, our verification provider, which checks that the document is valid and matches the face. Yadony does not receive these images: only the verification result and the verified name, which is the one shown to the other party. By default, a traveller only accepts verified senders.

escrow.title: Payment held until delivery
escrow.text: By card, your payment is authorised when you send your request and charged when the traveller accepts it. The money then stays on the platform: the traveller only receives it after delivery is confirmed with the recipient's code. If the traveller declines, or the shipment is cancelled before handover, you get a full refund, fee included. If you choose to pay in cash, the money changes hands directly: this hold does not apply, and only the scan history remains.

cap.title: Capped refunds
cap.text: In case of proven loss or damage, Yadony may refund the shipment, up to a cap and under the conditions shown in the app when you post it. Beyond that, a parcel carried by an individual is no longer the right channel, and a professional carrier is a better fit. The fee does not include any parcel insurance.

tracking.title: Scans, a code, and the proof that comes with them
tracking.text: Handover, optional transit, arrival, delivery. The handover scan and the code-based delivery are required; transit is optional. Each step records the time and location, with a photo at handover and at delivery. This history is not decorative: it is the evidence a dispute is decided on. The sender and recipient can see it at all times, and it cannot be altered afterwards.

dispute.title: Dispute procedure
dispute.text: A dispute is opened from the app, within 15 days of the planned date, as soon as a step does not go as planned. The payout to the traveller is suspended during the review. We examine the scan history, the time-stamped photos and the in-app messages, then rule within 72 business hours: refund to the sender, payout to the traveller, or a split. The decision is reasoned and shared with both parties.

data.title: Your data
data.text: ID documents and selfies are processed by Didit, our verification provider, which hosts its data in the European Union. Yadony keeps no copy of them. The other party to a shipment sees your first name, your profile photo, your verification status and the details of the parcel concerned, nothing more. Shipment data is kept as long as needed to handle any dispute, then archived. The details are in the privacy policy.

limits.title: What we do not guarantee
limits.text: We do not carry parcels: the parcel stays in a traveller's luggage, subject to the ups and downs of their flight and airline. A flight delay, a strike or a customs check are outside our control. We do not search parcels for you: the traveller checks the contents at handover, and the sender is accountable for their declaration. We are not an insurer either: the fee includes no parcel insurance, and any refund remains capped. What we do guarantee is narrower and easier to verify: paid by card, the money is not released to the traveller until delivery is confirmed, and a dispute is decided on time-stamped evidence. Finally, a shipment arranged outside the app gives no recourse: without scans and without a payment through the platform, there is no record and no leverage.

seo.title: About yadony
seo.description: Why we built yadony: the story of a problem the diaspora has been solving for thirty years in WhatsApp groups, with no record of any of it.

about.title: Why we ended up building it
paragraphs: There is a message everyone in the diaspora has already written, or read: "is anyone flying to Abidjan this week?". Yadony was born from that message.

It happens in a WhatsApp group of two hundred people. Someone answers, you swap numbers, you meet on a Saturday in a car park. You hand a box to a stranger vouched for by a cousin, you pay in cash, and you wait. Most of the time, it works. It works remarkably well, in fact: that is how clothes, school supplies, spare parts and presents have been moving for thirty years.

The problem only shows up the day it does not work. The parcel does not arrive. The number stops answering. There is no record, no proof of handover, no receipt, nobody to call. You cannot even say what happened: lost, forgotten, kept. And because the person was doing you a favour, you do not dare push. You lose the parcel, and often you lose the relationship as well.

On the other side, there are the carriers. They are reliable, they are considerably more expensive, and they do not deliver everywhere. To get five kilos to someone you know, that is not a solution, it is giving up.

yadony is not trying to replace the traveller with a lorry. The traveller already exists, is already leaving, and their suitcase is already half empty. What was missing was not transport: it was a record. Knowing who carries what, when, and being able to prove it. Hence identity checks, scans at every step, time-stamped photos, the delivery code, and a payment that only reaches the traveller once the parcel is in the recipient's hands.

We started from the trips the diaspora already makes, between Paris, Lyon, Marseille and Abidjan, Dakar, Bamako or Douala, and the app now accepts any departure and arrival city. We have no numbers to show off: we are just starting, and the app is still in beta. If you use it and something feels off, write to us. At this stage, it is the most useful feedback we could get.

cgu.title: Terms of use
cgu.intro: YADONY SAS ("Yadony") publishes a mobile and web application connecting travellers leaving France for West Africa with senders wishing to send parcels to their relatives. Yadony secures these exchanges through identity verification, payment held until delivery, and parcel traceability at every step. These Terms of Use apply to any use of the platform. Signing up constitutes acceptance of these Terms. If you do not accept them, you must not use the platform. This English version is provided for convenience; the French version prevails.

p: The application is open to any adult (18 or over) with the capacity to contract. One account per phone number.
Every user can both send parcels and carry them. There is no role to choose at sign-up: both possibilities are available to everyone from account creation.

Before posting a trip or a parcel request, every user must verify their identity with our provider Didit: a photo of their ID document and a selfie. The result is usually known within minutes. Verified accounts display the "Identity verified" badge.

articles.title: Article 2. What Yadony does (and does not do)

p: Yadony is an intermediary. It connects travellers and senders, secures payments and provides tracking and dispute-management tools. Yadony is not a carrier: it does not physically transport parcels.
Travellers are private individuals or transport professionals.
Yadony operates on international corridors between Europe, the United States, Canada and Africa. The list of available corridors can be consulted in the application and may change.

Any verified traveller can publish a listing. It must state the route, departure date, available kilos (1 to 30 kg), price per kilo, the handover and pick-up locations (with the geographic area and practical arrangements), and the accepted payment methods.
You can create listing templates and schedule recurring trips (automatic publication according to your calendar).

A listing can be edited as long as no request has been accepted. If you delete it, pending requests are automatically declined and the senders concerned are informed. If senders had already paid, they are refunded in full, automatically. In that case the traveller must return any parcels already handed over: the application generates a return code the traveller must enter to confirm the sender has recovered their parcel. Until that code is validated, the traveller's account is blocked.
To send a parcel, you fill in a form: weight, description of the contents, photos, declared value (maximum €500) and the recipient's details.
Before confirming, you electronically sign a warning about prohibited goods and your customs liability. That signature is kept as evidence.
The traveller reviews your full declaration before accepting. If they find at handover that the contents do not match, they can refuse the parcel without penalty. You are then refunded automatically.
The following items may not be sent:
ul: Drugs, narcotics or illicit substances
Weapons, explosives or hazardous materials
Counterfeits or goods prohibited by customs
Live animals
Official documents (passports, identity cards, residence permits)
Any item whose transport, import or export is prohibited or subject to special authorisation under the law of the departure country, destination country or any transit country

p: When a sender submits a request compatible with your listing, you receive a notification. You accept or decline (reason optional). If you accept, you set a handover appointment: a place and a time slot of 4 hours maximum.
If you do not confirm your presence as the appointment approaches, the sender receives an alert 2 hours before.
Price negotiation happens directly in the application. All offers and counter-offers are recorded.

At handover, the traveller scans the parcel's QR code (DON-XXXXXX format) and takes a photo. The parcel is then scanned at three stages: Departure, Transit and Arrival. Every scan is timestamped and geolocated.

The sender follows the journey in real time in the application. The recipient in the destination country can track the parcel from a simple web page, with no account or application, even on a basic phone with a slow connection.
If the traveller has no network (airport, plane), scans are stored and sent automatically as soon as the connection returns.
Payments are processed by licensed providers. Yadony never stores card numbers. You can pay by:
ul: Bank card (Visa, Mastercard), Apple Pay or Google Pay via Stripe
Mobile Money: Wave and Orange Money
Yadony wallet (balance top-up in the application)

p: Any payment made outside the platform is prohibited. The messaging system automatically blocks attempts to exchange contact details to bypass Yadony.
Biometric validation (fingerprint, Face ID or PIN code) is optional before any payment.
As soon as you pay, the money is immediately held by Stripe. No one can touch it before delivery is confirmed.
Delivery is confirmed by the recipient: they enter a 6-digit code received by SMS on the tracking page. The traveller is paid within the following 24 hours.
If the recipient does not confirm within 48 hours, the Yadony team can release the payment manually, only after a check. That action is logged. An honest traveller never waits indefinitely.

Yadony charges a service commission on each transaction, at the rate in force shown before payment. It is deducted automatically. In the event of a refund, the commission is never kept: you get back everything you paid.
If the traveller cancels their trip: automatic full refund of all senders (3 to 5 business days). Yadony offers you a replacement traveller within 72 hours.
If the sender cancels before handover, they are refunded in full.

The wallet is topped up by bank card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. It can also receive free credits: referral rewards and amounts credited back to the wallet by Yadony, for example after cancelling a parcel paid with the wallet.
Every payment made with the wallet uses free credits first, then topped-up money, starting with the most recent top-up.

You can at any time request a refund of topped-up money you have not spent, from the Wallet screen in the application. It is paid back to the payment method used for the top-up, within 5 to 10 business days depending on your bank. A partly spent top-up is refunded for the remaining part. While the request is in progress, the balance in that currency cannot be used.
If the refund to the original payment method fails (expired card, top-up too old, refusal by the payment provider), the Yadony team refunds the amount concerned by another means.
Free credits are neither refundable nor convertible into cash. They can only be used to pay for parcels on Yadony.
After each delivery, the sender and the traveller can rate each other (1 to 5 stars plus a comment), within 7 days. The recipient can also rate the traveller from the web page, without an account.
Ratings must reflect a real experience. Yadony automatically detects fake ratings and excludes them from the average.
This badge distinguishes reliable travellers. It is granted to travellers who have:
ul: At least 5 confirmed deliveries
An average rating of 4.0 or higher over the last 5 deliveries
No active suspension
Deliveries made to at least 5 different recipients, at least 7 days apart (to prevent gaming)

p: Travellers who work the route regularly (several times a month) can access the Yadony PRO web space. It offers a full dashboard: recurring-trip management with automatic publication, automations, rate cards, a pricing assistant, tax export and activity statistics.
Access is reserved for PRO accounts. A regular traveller can request an upgrade to a PRO account from the application.
You have 48 hours after delivery to report a problem through the application. After that, the delivery is deemed compliant and the traveller is paid.

The Yadony team holds all the evidence: scans, photos, messages, signed declaration. It notifies the traveller within 24 hours and issues a decision within 72 hours at most. In case of disagreement, Yadony decides on evidence, not on word.

In the event of proven loss or damage, Yadony may refund up to €50 per incident (internal guarantee fund), within the limit of the declared value. Excluded from the guarantee: undeclared or prohibited contents, the absence of a geolocated delivery photo, and disputes reported late.
A sender who opens 3 disputes without evidence is suspended automatically.
If the dispute is not resolved to your satisfaction, you can turn free of charge to an approved consumer mediator.
Yadony includes several automatic protections:
ul: One phone number = one account
Detection of accounts sharing the same bank details
Automatic filtering of messages attempting to exchange contact details to bypass the platform
Automatic suspension after 2 parcels refused for non-compliant contents
Detection of fake ratings (the same people rating each other, series of 5 stars with no comment)
A tamper-proof log of all sensitive actions

p: Yadony: responsible for the proper operation of the platform and the escrow. Yadony is not responsible for the contents of parcels, for damage during transport, or for users' actions.
The traveller: responsible for the parcel from the departure scan until delivery is confirmed. In the event of loss or damage, their liability is engaged up to the declared value.
The sender: responsible for the compliance of their parcel. Any false declaration engages their sole liability, including in the event of customs or criminal proceedings.
Yadony is an intermediation platform. Income received by travellers through the application (payments received for carrying parcels) is personal income falling under their own tax responsibility.

Each traveller is solely responsible for declaring their income to the competent tax authorities of their country of residence, in accordance with applicable local law. Yadony provides no tax advice and assumes no responsibility for non-declaration or incorrect declaration of income generated through the platform.

The Yadony PRO space provides professional travellers with an export of their transaction history for personal accounting purposes. This tool is provided for information only and does not constitute tax assistance.
Yadony complies with the European General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). For any question: dpo{'@'}yadony.com.

We collect only the data needed to run the service: identity (KYC), contact details, transaction data, delivery photos and browsing data. We never store your bank details (handled directly by Stripe). Images of your ID document and your face are processed by Didit, our verification provider: Yadony keeps no copy of them.

Your data is kept for as long as you use your account plus 3 years. Transaction data is kept for 5 years (statutory accounting obligation). Identity documents are kept for 5 years after your relationship with Yadony ends.

You can at any time view, edit, export or delete your data from the application settings. When an account is deleted: profile data anonymised, identity documents erased, recipient address book cleared (except payment history, kept for 5 years).
For any unresolved complaint, you can contact the CNIL: www.cnil.fr.

As part of the corridors to West Africa, some data may be transferred to Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Mali or Cameroon. These transfers are governed by the mechanisms provided for by the GDPR. Photos and documents are stored on European servers.

Yadony sends you notifications through the application (primary channel) and by SMS (backup channel). For the 3 critical events (payment received, delivery confirmed, dispute opened), if your phone does not acknowledge receipt within 60 seconds, an SMS is sent automatically. Two different SMS operators ensure continuity in case of outage.

seo.title: Privacy policy
seo.description: How Yadony protects your data: minimal internal data, certified partners (Firebase, Stripe, Cloudflare), retention periods and GDPR rights.

confidentialite.title: Privacy policy
confidentialite.intro: Yadony is a mobile marketplace connecting travellers with spare luggage space to senders wishing to send parcels to their relatives. Our service covers corridors from Europe, the United States, Canada and Africa to all the destinations we serve. We designed Yadony around one core principle: we keep only the strict minimum of personal data internally. Sensitive data (identity, authentication, official documents) is entrusted to trusted, globally recognised specialised partners who process it with a level of security and compliance we could not reach alone. By using Yadony, you accept the practices described in this document. This English version is provided for convenience; the French version prevails.

articles.title: 1. Who is responsible for your data?

p: Data controller: YADONY SAS, a simplified joint-stock company whose registration is in progress.
Data Protection Officer (DPO): dpo{'@'}yadony.com. General contact: contact{'@'}yadony.com.
If you have a question about your data or wish to exercise your rights, contact us directly. We undertake to reply within a reasonable time.

articles.title: 2. Our core principle: as little data as possible

p: Yadony stores internally only the information needed for your user profile. All sensitive data (identity, authentication, official documents, images) is processed and stored directly by specialised partners. Yadony never sees your identity documents, your face, or your bank details.
The only data stored in our own systems is your public profile information:
ul: First and last name: displaying your identity on your profile and in transactions
E-mail address: identifying you and sending you transaction summaries
Date of birth: verifying that you are an adult (18 minimum)
City of residence: making it easier to match you with travellers near you

p: That is all. Yadony stores no other personal data internally. The rest is handled by our specialised partners, described below.

articles.title: 3. Our partners and the data they handle for us

p: We chose to entrust each type of sensitive data to the world specialist in that field. Here is exactly who handles what.

blocks.sub: 3.1 Google Firebase: authentication and account security
p: The entire authentication layer is handled by Google Firebase, one of the most secure infrastructures in the world. Firebase handles:
ul: Your mobile phone number
Your SMS sign-in (one-time code)
Your fingerprint and Face ID sign-in
Your session security (suspicious sign-in detection, lockout after failed attempts)
Your backup PIN code

p: Yadony never sees your full phone number or your biometric data. Firebase manages this information directly, in line with its own privacy policy and Google's security certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR). Google Firebase privacy policy: https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy

Identity verification, required to post a trip or a parcel request, is handled by Didit (Didit Identity Spain, S.L., Barcelona, Spain), which acts as Yadony's processor under the GDPR and hosts its data in the European Union. Didit handles:
ul: The photo of your identity document (national ID card or passport)
The selfie and the liveness check
The comparison between your face and your official document
The approval or rejection of the verification

p: Yadony receives neither your identity documents nor images of your face. Didit sends us the verification result (Verified, Under review or Declined, with the reason for a decline) and, for a successful check, your name as it appears on the document. Didit keeps documents and biometric data according to the retention settings defined by Yadony and its own policy. Didit privacy policy: https://didit.me/terms/privacy-policy/
All payments, the escrow mechanism (money held until delivery) and payouts to travellers are handled exclusively by Stripe. Stripe handles:
ul: Your bank card details (Visa, Mastercard)
Apple Pay and Google Pay payments
Holding funds in escrow until delivery is confirmed
Payouts to travellers after delivery
Refunds in the event of cancellation or dispute

p: Yadony never stores your card number or any payment data. Stripe is PCI DSS Level 1 certified, the highest security certification for online payments. Stripe privacy policy: https://stripe.com/fr/privacy

blocks.sub: 3.4 Wave and Orange Money: Mobile Money
p: For Mobile Money payments and payouts (mainly for users and travellers based in Africa), we rely on Wave and Orange Money. These providers manage your Mobile Money account details directly. Yadony does not store this information.
All parcel-related images (photos taken by the sender, handover and delivery photos taken by the traveller) are stored on Cloudflare infrastructure. Cloudflare handles:
ul: Secure storage of parcel photos
Timestamped, geolocated handover and delivery photos
Generation of temporary, secure access links: images are never permanently publicly accessible

p: Yadony does not host these images on its own servers. Cloudflare is one of the world leaders in web security and performance, certified ISO 27001 and SOC 2. Cloudflare privacy policy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

articles.title: 4. Data generated by your use of the service

p: Beyond profile data and the data handled by our partners, Yadony generates and keeps the following data, essential to running the service:
ul: History of listings and trips: managing traveller activity and producing tax exports for Yadony PRO. Retention: 5 years
Transaction history (amounts, dates, statuses): financial traceability and statutory accounting obligations. Retention: 5 years (legal obligation)
Parcel scans (timestamp and geolocation): parcel traceability at every step and evidence in disputes. Retention: 5 years
Ratings and reviews received: building user reputation and guaranteeing quality. Retention: lifetime of the account
Messages exchanged in the internal messaging system: enabling communication between senders and travellers. Retention: 2 years after the transaction
Connection data (date, device, anonymised): account security and fraud detection. Retention: 13 months

p: Browsing and app-usage data is collected in anonymised form only, and only with your explicit consent gathered at your first sign-in.
Here is a complete summary to give you a clear picture of how your data is protected.
ul: Name, e-mail, date of birth, city: Yadony (internal database). Yadony access: yes, profile data only
Phone number, SMS authentication: Google Firebase. Yadony access: no, Firebase manages it directly
Fingerprint, Face ID, PIN code: Google Firebase. Yadony access: no, biometric data stays on-device or with Firebase
ID document photo, selfie, liveness: Didit. Yadony access: no, Yadony receives only the verification result and the verified name
Card number, payment data: Stripe. Yadony access: no, never sent to Yadony
Mobile Money details: Wave / Orange Money. Yadony access: no, managed directly by those services
Parcel and delivery photos: Cloudflare. Access only through secure temporary links
Transaction history, scans, ratings: Yadony (internal database). Access: yes, needed to run the service
Messages between users: Yadony (encrypted). Encrypted content, access restricted to disputes

articles.title: 6. The legal basis for each processing operation

ul: Profile data (name, e-mail, date of birth, city): performance of the contract (Terms of Use)
Authentication via Google Firebase: performance of the contract
Identity verification via Didit: legal obligation (anti-money-laundering and fraud prevention)
Payment processing and escrow via Stripe: performance of the contract
Image storage via Cloudflare: performance of the contract and legitimate interest (evidence in disputes)
Transaction history: legal obligation (accounting and tax)
Parcel scans and traceability: performance of the contract and legitimate interest
Fraud detection and security: legitimate interest
Ratings and reputation: legitimate interest
Marketing communications: consent (revocable at any time)
p: Each processing operation rests on a specific legal basis:

articles.title: 7. Who do we share your data with?

p: Yadony never sells your data to third parties. The only data sharing that takes place is described in sections 3 and 4 above, with our technical partners contractually committed to protecting it.

ul: Between users: your first name, profile photo, rating and badge are visible to other users as part of the normal service.
With the authorities: where the law requires it (judicial requisition, tax obligation, anti-money-laundering), we must disclose certain data to the competent authorities.
In a dispute: the relevant evidence (scans, link to the Cloudflare photos, messages) may be shared between the parties involved.
Business transfer: in the event of a merger or acquisition, your data could be transferred to the acquirer. You would be informed beforehand.
p: Beyond those partners:
Yadony operates on international corridors and relies on global partners. Here is how your data is protected in each region.

The data Yadony keeps directly is hosted on servers located in the European Union. Our partners (Google Firebase, Stripe, Cloudflare) all have GDPR-compliant transfer mechanisms (standard contractual clauses, adequacy decisions or EU-US Data Privacy Framework certifications).

blocks.sub: From the United States and Canada
p: For users based in the United States and Canada, we comply with applicable local laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) for Californian users. Yadony does not sell your data. You can exercise your rights by contacting us at dpo{'@'}yadony.com.

For users based in Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, Mali, Cameroon and the other countries served, we comply with the applicable local personal-data protection laws. Parcel images and documents are always stored on Cloudflare (European servers), with temporary, secure access links.

articles.title: 9. How long do we keep your data?

ul: Profile data (name, e-mail, date of birth, city): for as long as you use the service plus 3 years after your last sign-in, for account management
Authentication data (Firebase): managed by Google Firebase under its own policy
KYC data (Didit): kept by Didit according to the settings defined by Yadony and Didit's policy
Payment data (Stripe): managed by Stripe under its own policy
Parcel images (Cloudflare): 5 years, temporary links, evidence in disputes
Transaction history: 5 years, accounting and tax obligation
Scans and geolocation: 5 years, evidence in disputes
Messages in the messaging system: 2 years after the transaction, dispute resolution
Anonymised browsing data: 13 months, CNIL compliance
Deleted accounts: profile data anonymised immediately, except financial history kept for 5 years
p: Retention periods by type of data:

Yadony's main security mechanism is architectural: by keeping only the minimum of data internally and entrusting sensitive data to certified global specialists, we drastically reduce the exposure surface if something goes wrong.
ul: Google Firebase: certified ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, PCI DSS. Authentication data encrypted and isolated.
Didit: ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 certified, data hosted in the European Union. Identity documents encrypted, never passed on to Yadony.
Cloudflare: certified ISO 27001, SOC 2. Images accessible only through secure temporary links.
Yadony: profile data encrypted at rest and in transit (HTTPS/TLS). Internal access limited to the strict minimum.
Every sensitive action (payment release, dispute decision, account suspension) is recorded in a tamper-proof audit log.
Biometric validation (fingerprint or Face ID via Firebase) is required to access the application and confirm any payment.
The internal messaging system automatically filters attempts to share contact details to bypass the platform.
In the event of a data breach, we notify the CNIL within 72 hours and the users concerned as soon as possible.
p: Safeguards complete this architecture:

ul: Right of access: obtain a copy of all the data Yadony holds about you, via Settings → My data or dpo{'@'}yadony.com
Right of rectification: correct your profile data (name, e-mail, city), directly in your profile in the application
Right to erasure: delete your account and profile data, via Settings → Delete my account
Right to portability: receive your data in JSON or CSV format, on request to dpo{'@'}yadony.com
Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interest, on request to dpo{'@'}yadony.com
Withdrawal of consent: turn off marketing or analytics, via Settings → Privacy
Rights over Firebase data: access, rectification, deletion of authentication data, through your Google account or dpo{'@'}yadony.com
Rights over Stripe data: access to and deletion of payment and identity data, via stripe.com/fr or dpo{'@'}yadony.com
p: Your rights and how to exercise them:
For data handled by our partners (Firebase, Stripe, Cloudflare), we help you exercise your rights with them. Contact us at dpo{'@'}yadony.com and we will make the connection.
If you are not satisfied with the answer: CNIL (www.cnil.fr) in France, ARTCI in Côte d'Ivoire, CDP in Senegal, the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data in Cameroon.

Yadony uses only the cookies strictly necessary to run the application (session persistence, security). Audience-measurement cookies are enabled only with your explicit consent and the data collected is anonymised. You can manage your preferences from Settings → Privacy and data.

Transactional notifications (mandatory): payment confirmation, delivery confirmed, dispute opened, security alerts. Sent through Firebase Cloud Messaging (in-app notifications) and by SMS through two different operators to guarantee continuity.
Marketing communications (optional): sent only with your consent. You can unsubscribe at any time from Settings → Notifications.

Yadony is strictly reserved for adults (18 and over). We collect no data about minors. If you believe a minor has created an account, contact us at dpo{'@'}yadony.com. We will delete the account and all associated data as quickly as possible.

articles.title: 15. What happens when you delete your account

ul: Yadony profile data (first name, last name, e-mail, date of birth, city): anonymised immediately.
Firebase data (phone, authentication): deleted on request through Firebase.
Didit data (ID document, selfie): deleted according to the retention settings Yadony has defined with Didit.
Parcel images (Cloudflare): the links become inaccessible. Files are deleted under Cloudflare's policy.
Messages in the messaging system: deleted.
Recipient address book: cleared.
Transaction history: kept for 5 years (statutory accounting obligation). This data is anonymised as far as possible.
If a dispute is in progress, the account is kept until the dispute is closed, then deleted.
p: When you delete your account:

We may change this policy at any time. Any significant change will be notified by e-mail or in-app notification at least 30 days before it takes effect. The update date is always shown at the top of the document.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: This page describes what yadony.com stores on your device, why, and how to stay in control.

what.title: What a cookie is
what.text: A cookie is a small file a website places on your device to remember information between visits. The browser's local storage plays a comparable role.

current.title: What yadony.com uses today
current.text: This site sets no advertising cookie and no third-party tracker. Traffic is measured with Cloudflare Web Analytics, a cookieless tool: it stores nothing on your device, creates no identifier, does not follow visitors from site to site, and only collects aggregate statistics (page views, country, device type). This kind of measurement is exempt from consent under CNIL guidance. The only information stored on your device is your answer to the banner, kept in your browser's local storage.

storage.title: Duration and scope
storage.text: Your choice stays on your device until you delete it, and is never sent to our servers or to third parties. Cloudflare Web Analytics statistics are anonymous and aggregated: they cannot identify you. If we ever add a tool that sets cookies or tracks visitors, this page will be updated and your consent requested before anything is activated.

seo.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Dakar with a verified traveller
seo.description: A verified traveller already flying to Dakar carries your parcel: per-kilo price set by the traveller, payment held until delivery, QR-code tracking.

parisDakar.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Dakar
parisDakar.lead: Paris–Dakar is Yadony's most active corridor: the Senegalese community of the Paris region sends parcels to Dakar every week, and travellers fly the route in both directions all year round.
parisDakar.how: Publish your parcel in the app with its weight, description and photo. Verified travellers flying from Paris to Dakar see your request and offer their price per kilo. You choose, hand the parcel over in person in the Paris region, and your relative collects it in Dakar from the traveller.
parisDakar.price: The price per kilo is set freely by each traveller according to their flight and baggage allowance. You compare listings before choosing. A service commission, always shown before payment, is deducted from the transaction.
parisDakar.delay: A direct Paris–Dakar flight takes about 5.5 hours. Your parcel arrives on the day of the traveller's flight: from handover, you know the exact date, and the pick-up in Dakar is arranged in the days after landing.
parisDakar.safety: Traveller identity verified with Didit, card payment held until delivery is confirmed, handover validated with a 6-digit code, every step time-stamped and geolocated. Your loved one follows everything from a simple web page, no account needed.

faq.question: How much does sending a parcel Paris–Dakar cost?
faq.answer: The traveller sets their price per kilo; you compare listings before choosing. For a 5 kg parcel with a traveller at 8 euros per kilo, the traveller receives 40 euros and you pay 40 euros plus the service fee, shown before payment.

faq.question: How long does a parcel take to reach Dakar?
faq.answer: The traveller's flight time (about 5.5 hours direct), plus the handover appointment in Dakar. You see the departure date before booking, so you know from the start when your parcel arrives.

faq.question: How does my relative collect the parcel in Dakar?
faq.answer: The traveller and the recipient agree on a meeting. At handover, the recipient gives the 6-digit code you passed on to them and the traveller takes a photo: delivery is confirmed and the traveller's payment is released.

seo.title: Send a parcel from Lyon to Abidjan with a verified traveller
seo.description: Entrust your parcel to a verified traveller flying from Lyon to Abidjan: transparent per-kilo price, escrow until delivery, QR-code tracking.

lyonAbidjan.title: Send a parcel from Lyon to Abidjan
lyonAbidjan.lead: The Ivorian community of Lyon and its region no longer needs to go through Paris: travellers connect Lyon directly to Abidjan, and your parcel rides in their suitcase.
lyonAbidjan.how: Describe your parcel in the app: weight, contents, photos. Verified travellers leaving from Lyon (or Paris if you want more options) offer their price. Once accepted, you hand over the parcel in person and every step is tracked all the way to Abidjan.
lyonAbidjan.price: Each traveller advertises their price per kilo; for parcels of a few kilos it is often better value than a classic carrier, and you know exactly who is carrying. The service commission is shown before you confirm.
lyonAbidjan.delay: Allow about 6.5 hours for a direct Lyon–Abidjan flight. The parcel arrives with the traveller: the date is known at booking time, with no vague multi-week window.
lyonAbidjan.safety: Mandatory identity check, card payment held until the recipient confirms, time-stamped and geolocated scans. If something goes wrong, you have 15 days to open a dispute, settled within 72 business hours on evidence.

faq.question: Are there often travellers between Lyon and Abidjan?
faq.answer: Lyon–Abidjan is one of Yadony's launch corridors. If no traveller departs from Lyon on your dates, the app also shows departures from Paris to Abidjan to widen the choice.

faq.question: What can I send to Abidjan?
faq.answer: Anything legal and declared: clothes, non-regulated medicines, non-official documents, everyday products. Prohibited items include drugs, weapons, counterfeits, live animals and identity documents. The traveller sees your full declaration before accepting.

faq.question: How is the payment protected?
faq.answer: By card, you are charged when the traveller accepts, but the money stays held on the platform: the traveller is only paid after delivery is confirmed, with the 6-digit code you pass on to the recipient. If the shipment is cancelled before handover, you get a full refund.

seo.title: Send a parcel from Marseille to Bamako with a verified traveller
seo.description: A verified traveller flying from Marseille to Bamako carries your parcel: price set by the traveller, payment held until delivery, full tracking.

marseilleBamako.title: Send a parcel from Marseille to Bamako
marseilleBamako.lead: From Marseille and the whole south of France, the Malian community sends parcels to Bamako without detours: a traveller already making the trip carries them, with real tracking at every step.
marseilleBamako.how: Create your request in the app with the weight and a description of the parcel. A verified traveller flying from Marseille to Bamako accepts it, you agree on a handover meeting together, and the parcel is scanned at handover then delivered against the recipient's code.
marseilleBamako.price: The price per kilo is the one the traveller advertises: no hidden rate card, no surprises at a counter. A service commission is deducted from the transaction, shown before payment.
marseilleBamako.delay: The Marseille–Bamako flight takes about 5.5 hours direct. Your parcel arrives the day the traveller lands; delivery to the recipient follows at the appointment agreed in the app.
marseilleBamako.safety: Every traveller verifies their identity with Didit, ID document and selfie, before they can post a trip. Paid by card, the money stays held until the recipient's confirmation code, and the scan history is the reference in any dispute.

faq.question: How much does a Marseille–Bamako shipment cost?
faq.answer: The traveller sets their price per kilo and you see it before booking. Example: 5 kg at 8 euros per kilo, the traveller receives 40 euros and you pay 40 euros plus the service fee, shown before payment.

faq.question: Does my relative in Bamako need to install the app?
faq.answer: No. The recipient follows the parcel from a simple web page, even on a basic phone with a slow connection. At handover, they give the traveller the 6-digit code you passed on to them.

faq.question: What if the traveller cancels their trip?
faq.answer: You get a full, automatic refund, fee included, and the app suggests other travellers leaving around the same dates.

seo.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Douala with a verified traveller
seo.description: Send parcels to Cameroon with a verified traveller from Paris to Douala: clear price per kilo, payment held until delivery, handover validated with a code.

parisDouala.title: Send a parcel from Paris to Douala
parisDouala.lead: For the Cameroonian diaspora, Paris–Douala is the most direct path: a verified traveller on that flight carries your parcel and your family collects it in person, proof of delivery included.
parisDouala.how: Publish the parcel in the app: weight, contents, photos, the recipient's details in Douala. A verified traveller accepts it, you hand it over in the Paris region, and you follow the scans through to final delivery, photo included.
parisDouala.price: The price depends on the traveller and their baggage allowance: each one advertises a per-kilo rate and you choose. The service commission is deducted from the transaction and always shown before you pay.
parisDouala.delay: About 6.5 hours of direct flight Paris–Douala. The arrival date is the traveller's flight date, known before booking, so you can tell your family the exact day from the start.
parisDouala.safety: Identities verified with Didit, card payment held until the recipient's confirmation code, every step tracked from Paris to Douala. The recipient follows everything from a web page, no account needed.

faq.question: Can I send a parcel to Yaoundé instead of Douala?
faq.answer: The corridor serves Douala, where the traveller lands. Final delivery happens at the appointment agreed between the traveller and your recipient; if your relative is in Yaoundé, they can arrange a meeting point with the traveller, but the reference delivery city remains Douala.

faq.question: What happens if the parcel is lost?
faq.answer: Open a dispute from the app within 15 days of the planned date. The payout to the traveller is suspended, the team reviews the evidence, and Yadony may refund the shipment, up to a cap and under the conditions shown in the app.

faq.question: How do I know where my parcel is?
faq.answer: The traveller scans the parcel at handover, may add a transit scan, marks their arrival, and delivery is then validated with the recipient's code. Each step is time-stamped and geolocated, and you and the recipient see the same tracking page in real time.

faq.question: Are there Paris–Abidjan travellers all year round?
faq.answer: It is Yadony's busiest corridor: daily flights between Paris and Abidjan and the size of the Ivorian community in France mean regular departures all year, not just around the holidays.

faq.question: Does my relative in Abidjan need to install the app?
faq.answer: No. The recipient follows the parcel from a simple web page, even on a basic phone. At handover, they give the traveller the 6-digit code you passed on to them: that is what confirms delivery and releases the traveller's payment.
